analysis: Only the test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift changed. The supplied units are BASE text, lines 3039-4237. The head additions (lines 3140-3240 per the file_changes range) are visible only as a truncated patch excerpt. Two new tests appear there: remembersHeaderVerdictsOnlyForUnchangedFiles and replacedLookalikeIsReadAgain. They exercise SSDWholeRootMaintainer.maintain caching of header-ownership verdicts, keyed on unchanged file identity. The first test covers a header rewritten to zeros with size and mtime restored, so only ctime changes; the file must lose its ownership proof and be left untouched. The second covers a malformed lookalike later replaced by a real block, which must be re-read and owned. Both are consistent with T-041 (retained cache storage threat). The new behavior is a fail-safe design: the maintainer never deletes files lacking DBK3 ownership proof, and the existing base tests (malformedLookalikePreserved, symlinkedRootIsNeverTraversed, tempCleanupUsesAgeAndExactOwnership) already enforce that. The test change adds no production attack surface, and I found no regression in it. The security-relevant production change is a verdict cache in the whole-root maintainer, which is not in my supplied batch. Integration should verify that its cache key includes ctime, inode, size and mtime, and that it is invalidated on replacement or rename. This could matter for T-041 TTL/LRU enforcement: a stale 'owned' verdict could cause deletion of a file that is no longer a valid block, and a stale 'not owned' verdict could leave expired ciphertext in place. The base units 3653-4237 (donation outcomes, window sidecar tests) are unchanged and show no security regression. The patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not verify the full set of new test assertions.
